versions.short: The bill would establish the Ralph David Abernathy, Sr., National Historic Site in Georgia as a unit of the National Park System, to preserve and explain the historic West Hunter Street Baptist Church, where Dr. Abernathy served as pastor during the modern civil rights movement, and his role as a civil rights leader. The site would not formally be established until the Secretary of the Interior determines that enough land has been acquired to make a manageable unit, and then the Secretary would publish notice in the Federal Register. The Secretary could acquire land within the boundary shown on a map by donation, purchase from willing sellers, or exchange, but state-owned land could only be acquired by donation. The Secretary would administer the site under the laws generally applicable to National Park System units and would have to complete a management plan within 3 years after funds first become available. The Secretary could also enter into agreements with the state or other entities for signage, exhibits, parking, interpretive technology, tours, and preservation of historic resources.
